channel.title: Comments for page "The Conspiracy Of Sigma 3"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The Conspiracy Of Sigma 3"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I never noticed the CYOA link before and thought the SH format was all this was. So I hated it.

I love what's in the CYOA, but I still think the initial article is a slog to get through; to quote what Petrograd said, "skillfully pulling off something I hate isn't going to stop me from hating it."

Downvote switched to Novote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is pretty terrific.

The first part was both fascinating and hilarious at times, and really adds depth and complexity to the Serpent's Hand as a GOI. The second part was weird and obscure, the writing dream-like, evocative. I loved the blending of science-fiction and fantasy elements, and the strange nostalgia that pervaded the text - I kept being reminded of the Tales of The Dying Earth (especially with the Green Pool episode).

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Dang. I mean, "crazy conspiracy theorist gets 99% of Sigma-3 wrong" was good enough for an upvote by itself. I haven't seen a Hand article like this before, and I loved it.

And then you went and did that… thing at the end. And, yeah, it's kind of vague and has a tendency to repeat itself, but it's cool. And worthy of an upvote by itself.

Which is why they combine into a downvote No, but this was great. :V

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wow, didn't think I'd see a format screw on the SH GoI format anytime soon. Fascinating.

I found this to be entertaining as it basically is the author's shouting about how bad the SCPF is for shutting down death cults and preventing the summoning of great old ones, and the rest of the readers rolling their eyes and moving on. The back and forth banter in the footnotes also really sells it.

I did go through the CYOA, but to be honest the content there wasn't really my cup of tea.

In the end, an enthusiastic upvote.

item.content:encoded:
Mmmm neutral vote. I'm still exploring the CYOA, which is quite interesting.

In the main article, though, you've pretty perfectly aped mystical internet conspiracy crazy talk, kicking off what I personally call The Crucible effect: skillfully pulling off something I hate isn't going to stop me from hating it.

Personal bias speaking, but that's where it is. Satanic numerology makes me want to punch things.

Edit: In any case, I enjoyed the twine quite a bit.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I was thoroughly engaged by the main document. The CYOA, while slower, was still full of interesting tidbits, and intriguing points of view. And, of course, all the writing is top notch. Good job.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I had no idea that I was ready for what is essentially a format screw of the SH format! And that's primarily a reference to the main article - I skimmed a few of the CYOA pages, but didn't find them as interesting as the main piece, which I upvoted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The tone here and in the "choose your own adventure" style narrative is really, really good. The panic and paranoia helps maintain a tension that keeps me interested in this story. The latter doubt section also provided some breakage necessary to not keep this too heavy.

The latter bit went extremely heavy. While this is often good, it also was too heavy at certain times. I felt as if it was reaching too hard to philosophy or conjecture without any real solid substance or actual significant/wise things to say. The tone however felt very solid/consistent throughout.

I enjoyed reading, even though at some points it struck me as overly dramatic.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This proves that one of the biggest strengths of the Serpent's Hand format lies not just in the main text, but in the footnotes and the way people interact with each other in natural ways. You don't just feel like these are people speaking; they're a community. And a group that's as disjointed in popular canon as the Hand needs that kind of community solidified, and these formats are honestly one of the best ways to accomplish that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A very interesting take on the Serpent Hand's format. They are usually used like catalogues and profiles, but it appears that the author repurposed it into a propaganda piece.

Contrary to A Random Day, this felt more like the work of those New World Order conspiracy theorist types.
